resources.string: The experimental model is only for studying the relative shape of curves. It cannot yet accurately predict your own serum estradiol level and must not be used to adjust your dose yourself.
Relative response over the last 48 hours: %1$s
Legacy PK: divided by its own response 1 h after 1 mg (sublingual tier of the latest record)
Experimental M2, candidate %1$s: divided by its own response 1 h after 1 mg
Band: range of the 15 frozen M2 candidates. This is the explored parameter set, not a 95% confidence interval, and it understates the uncertainty of the tail.
Shaded: more than 8 h since the latest dose. The shape of this tail is highly uncertain.
Each curve is normalized separately. Equal heights do not mean equal blood levels, and neither curve is in concentration units. Your concentration page is unchanged.
Candidates are listed by ID. Neither the order nor the default choice ranks accuracy.
Transit stages %1$s · fast input %2$s per h · elimination %3$s per h · slow input %4$s per h · slow share %5$s
Assumed background for reconstructing Price 1997: %1$s in that paper\'s units. A sensitivity assumption about that study only, not your baseline; it cannot be changed here.
Upper limit of the Rosano 1997 baseline used in fitting: %1$s in that paper\'s units.
Window: the last 48 hours, with no forecast and no planned doses. Doses up to 30 days before the window are added up; earlier ones are left out.
Sublingual estradiol doses used: %1$d · older doses left out: %2$d
settings at the time cannot be confirmed %1$d
What this page cannot tell you
It is not calibrated to you and has not been checked against independent people. Lab results are not used.
The share of slow absorption and the elimination rate cannot be told apart with the published data.
The curve more than about 8 to 24 hours after a dose is not reliable.
In retrospective cross-study tests M2 was not shown to do better than a simpler model. Neither curve is the accurate one.
Doses are added up linearly; this has not been verified in real individuals.
An area difference between Figure 1 and Table 1 of Price 1997 is still unexplained.
No records the experimental model can use

Only taken, non-deleted sublingual estradiol (E2) doses whose saved settings confirm the route and sublingual tier are used, from the 48-hour window and the 30 days before it. Oral estradiol, sublingual estradiol valerate and other routes are never used.
The experimental model could not be calculated for these records.
